=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of Seller Positions

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package is built to move almost all known risk to the Buyer. It combines a low general cap, a disclosure regime that discloses the whole data room, a knowledge bar on claims, and a post-completion treatment of known debts and defects. Together, these mean the Buyer could not recover for the matters the Seller has already identified, even though they total roughly AUD 4.1m against a AUD 4.8m general cap. The price mechanics and known items need to be fixed through the price and specific protections, not the warranty regime.

Two caveats: I have only the Seller's summary positions and disclosure letter, not the full draft SPA, and the clause cross-references in the Seller's note are inconsistent (for example, Riverlark appears as "Clause 2 / 7" in the summary but relates to change control at 8.1 and discharge at 9.2 in DD-003). Statutory points below should be confirmed by NSW counsel and the privacy and tax specialists.

---

## 1. Known issues: the central problem

The Seller's disclosures identify the following items:

| Item | Amount / exposure | Seller's treatment | Problem for Buyer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Riverlark facility | ~AUD 3.2m outstanding | Release "following Completion" | Debt-free deal: this should come out of the price at Completion |
| Employee Completion bonuses (DD-005) | AUD 420k + possible payroll tax / super on-costs | Not in funds flow; "a matter for the Seller" | Debt-like item; leaving it out shifts cost to Buyer |
| Ironquay SOW3 | AUD 180k open; no proof of payment | IP indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Project Materials may not transfer; indemnity too narrow |
| Sandbar renewals | AUD 330k (3 × AUD 110k) | "Ordinary course" | Looks like a single commitment split into three; not verified |
| Bluefen | ~AUD 3.6m revenue (~30%); consent not in hand | "Reasonable endeavours"; deemed satisfied on delivery of consent | Value at risk, with no protection |
| Privacy/export incident (DD-006) | ~1,240 records; scope and notification unknown | "Preliminary", "not expected to be material" | Potentially significant regulatory, notification and claim exposure |

Under the Seller's positions, the Buyer could not claim on these items because:
- Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything in the data room.
- Schedule 7 and Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2 disclose the whole data room and public registers against the warranties.
- Any recovery would be capped at AUD 4.8m, subject to a AUD 250k excess-only basket and an 18-month time limit.

**Position:** Known matters should be handled as (a) price or debt adjustments at Completion, (b) specific indemnities that sit outside the warranty regime, and (c) conditions or escrow where the outcome is unknown.

---

## 2. Issue-by-issue analysis and pushback

### General liability cap (Cl 12.1): 20% (AUD 4.8m)
- Low for a AUD 24m deal with known contingent exposure. Consider a general cap of at least 30–50% of price, with a separate higher cap or full price cap for fundamental and tax matters.
- The cap should not apply to fraud, fundamental warranties, tax indemnity or specific indemnities.

### Thresholds (Cl 12.2): de minimis AUD 25k, excess-only basket AUD 250k
- The excess-only basket means the Buyer bears the first AUD 250k of losses, which is a material transfer of risk.
- **Push for:** a tipping basket (once exceeded, the Buyer recovers from the first dollar), a lower basket (around 0.5% of price, roughly AUD 120k), and a de minimis that counts toward the basket, or a lower de minimis.
- Related claims arising from the same facts should be treated as one claim for threshold purposes.

### Time limits (Cl 12.3 / 13): 18 months for general warranties; limitation applies to all Claims
- 18 months is too short given the Bluefen consent timing, the privacy matter and any tax issues that may not surface until a later audit.
- The "applies to all Claims" wording would pull fundamental and tax claims into the 18-month limit.
- **Push for:** 24–36 months for general warranties; tax claims until 60 days after the relevant assessment or limitation period expires; fundamental warranties for at least the NSW contractual limitation period (six years under the Limitation Act 1969 (NSW), to be verified).

### Fundamental and title warranties subject to general caps and time limits
- **Reject.** Title, capacity and authority are foundational. They should be capped at the full price, with a limitation period at least as long as the statutory period.

### Exclusive remedy, non-reliance and limitations apply to "all Claims of any nature" (Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Reject as drafted.** Fraud, misleading conduct and deliberate concealment should be carved out. Under Australian law, a contractual term cannot exclude liability for a party's own fraud, and misleading or deceptive conduct protections in trade may not be fully excludable. Seek advice on the non-reliance wording so that it does not purport to exclude fraud or statutory claims.
- Exclusive-remedy language should not stop the Buyer claiming specific indemnities or pursuing a price adjustment mechanism.

### Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2): general disclosure of the data room and public registers
- **Reject.** Blanket disclosure of an entire data room, plus public registers, against the warranties would hollow out the warranty package.
- **Push for:** specific disclosure only, against specific warranties, with a fair-disclosure standard (the matter must be disclosed fairly and in sufficient detail to identify its nature and scope). Public registers should not qualify warranties except for matters that are expressly identified.
- Data room materials should be disclosed only if the Seller fairly discloses them in the disclosure letter.

### Buyer knowledge (Cl 8.3): no claim for matters known or discoverable
- **Reject.** This is an anti-sandbagging clause in its harshest form. The Buyer's knowledge should not bar a claim, and matters found in due diligence should be dealt with by specific indemnity or price adjustment.
- **Push for:** an express pro-sandbagging clause, stating that the Buyer's rights are not affected by its knowledge or by any investigation.

### Bluefen (Cl 3 / 6.3; DD-002; Disclosure 2)
- Bluefen represents roughly 30% of revenue, and the consent and its conditions in clause 11.3 are not satisfied.
- "Reasonable endeavours" should be "all reasonable endeavours", and the Seller should not be able to treat consent as satisfied merely on delivery of a counterparty consent. The condition should be satisfied only when the consent is unconditional or the conditions in 11.3 are met.
- **Push for:** consent as a condition precedent, a long-stop date, the Buyer's right to terminate if consent is not received, and a price adjustment or escrow if the Buyer waives the condition. If Bluefen terminates within a period after Completion, a specific indemnity or earn-out-style protection should apply.

### Riverlark (Cl 2 / 7; DD-003; Disclosure 3)
- The AUD 3.2m debt should be repaid at Completion from the purchase price. A post-completion release leaves the company exposed to the lender and the security holder.
- **Push for:** a payoff letter, discharge of all security (including PPSR registrations under the PPSR Act, to be checked), guarantee releases and the lender's consent to the change of control, all delivered at Completion and reflected in the funds flow.

### Ironquay (Cl 11.1; DD-004, DD-010; Disclosure 4)
- The indemnity should not be limited to the SOW3 payment. It should cover all IP ownership, transfer and licence defects relating to the Ironquay work.
- The condition in DD-004 clause 7.3 (transfer of Project Materials on payment of every SOW3 fee) must be satisfied, so the Buyer needs evidence of payment and a confirmatory assignment before Completion.
- **Push for:** a specific IP indemnity (not capped by the general cap or basket), and either payment before Completion or the AUD 180k deducted from the price.

### Employee bonuses (DD-005; Disclosure 5)
- Accrued and conditional Completion bonuses are debt-like items. They should be deducted from the price or paid by the Seller.
- Payroll tax and superannuation (currently 12% of ordinary time earnings) and any other on-costs should be quantified and borne by the Seller.
- **Push for:** inclusion in the funds flow, with a specific indemnity for any related tax or on-costs.

### Privacy / export incident (DD-006; Disclosure 6)
- The Seller describes the matter as preliminary and not expected to be material. Given that the date is now 5 November 2026, the Seller should already have assessed whether the matter is an eligible data breach under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth). If so, notification to the OAIC and affected individuals may already have been required, and the timing of that obligation should be confirmed.
- **Push for:** completion of the forensic investigation before signing, confirmation of whether notification is required, a specific indemnity for regulatory, notification, remediation and third-party claims (outside the cap and basket), a warranty on data security and no prior breaches, and confirmation of cyber insurance cover.

### Office lease (DD-007; Disclosure 7)
- Confirm whether the lease requires landlord consent to a change of control. If it does, obtain landlord consent or a waiver as a Completion deliverable.

### Supplier renewals (DD-008 / DD-011; Disclosure 8)
- Three renewals of AUD 110k each, read together, look like one AUD 330k commitment split into three. Check whether the aggregate amount is above any internal or contractual threshold.
- **Push for:** confirmation that the commitments are ordinary course, not prepayments or long commitments extending beyond Completion, and that the Seller bears any accrued pre-Completion portion. Consider treating unaccrued amounts as working capital adjustments.

### Mossvale (DD-009; Disclosure 9)
- The Seller says that the restriction on assignment is not triggered by a share sale. Confirm this against the full clause, including any change-of-control language.
- **Push for:** a legal opinion or waiver if there is any doubt, and a warranty that no consent is required.

### Title (DD-012; Disclosure 10)
- The share register is a Seller-controlled document and is not verification of title. It should be supported by an ASIC company extract, an encumbrance search, confirmation that there are no options or pre-emptive rights, and any issued share certificates.
- **Push for:** title and capacity as fundamental warranties, capped at the full price, with a limitation period at least as long as the statutory period.

### Tax and IP warranties ("settled under the general regime")
- Reject. Tax should be covered by a specific pre-Completion tax indemnity, outside the basket and de minimis, with a limitation period running until the relevant tax assessment period expires.
- IP warranties should be treated as fundamental for the Ironquay and core product IP.

---

## 3. Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1: Fix the known issues before signing**
1. Treat Riverlark (AUD 3.2m), bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs), Ironquay (AUD 180k) and any Sandbar commitments as debt-like items, deducted from the AUD 24m price and shown in the funds flow.
2. Replace the general "known matters" bar and data-room disclosure with specific indemnities for Ironquay IP, the privacy incident, the Bluefen revenue risk, the Sandbar renewals and tax.
3. Require a payoff letter and full security discharge for Riverlark at Completion.
4. Require a completed privacy assessment before signing.

**Priority 2: Reject the structural limits**
5. Delete clause 8.3 and insert a pro-sandbagging clause.
6. Narrow disclosure to specific, fairly disclosed matters against specific warranties.
7. Carve out fraud, fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities from the cap, basket, de minimis, time limits and exclusive-remedy provisions.
8. Remove the "applies to all Claims" limitation wording.

**Priority 3: Improve commercial terms**
9. Increase the general cap (aim for 30–50% of price) and set fundamental warranties at full price.
10. Replace the excess-only basket with a tipping basket at around 0.5% of price, and lower or aggregate the de minimis.
11. Extend general warranty claims to 24–36 months, with tax and fundamental claims running for the statutory or assessment periods.

**Priority 4: Conditions and deliverables**
12. Make Bluefen consent (with 11.3 conditions satisfied) a condition precedent, with a long-stop date and a price or escrow mechanism if waived.
13. Require landlord consent (if applicable), Mossvale confirmation, and independent title verification at Completion.
14. Require a bring-down of the disclosure letter and data room, because the current disclosure cut-off is 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago.

**Next steps:** Obtain the full Seller draft SPA to confirm clause numbering, and instruct NSW counsel to verify the statutory references (limitation periods, PPSR discharge, privacy notification timing, payroll tax and superannuation on-costs) before the mark-up goes out.
